clue.text: Unobtrusive stone well defaced

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

indicators.note: to deface here is to knock off the face, the front letter of the word for well

parts.note: being well means being in good health

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks past a vandalised stone well without being noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaced' strips the H from the front of HEALTHY, leaving EALTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy movement is quiet and furtive, designed not to draw notice, which is what unobtrusive conduct does.

clue.text: Silver stolen from barbarian hoard

indicators.note: the symbol for silver is taken away from the word for barbarian

parts.note: a savage is a brutal, uncivilised person
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver is plundered from a barbarian's treasure trove.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to put by or keep for later, which is to save.

clue.text: Realise female's forgotten how to make an impression

indicators.note: forgotten means the letter is left out

parts.note: to fetch a price is to realise it at sale
F stands for female; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman realises she can no longer remember how to impress people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realise' means sell for, as an item fetches a price. 'how to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching cuts lines into a surface, literally leaving a mark or imprint on it.

clue.text: Uneasily eye occult characters in cell

indicators.note: uneasily suggests the letters are disturbed and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eyes occult symbols in a prison cell with unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' links: the letters are the characters. 'cell' suggests a prison but is biological.
explanation.definitionFit: A leucocyte is a white blood cell, part of the body's immune system.

clue.text: Tudor in style, like Long John's walk?

definitions.meaning: built in the Tudor manner with an exposed wooden frame
Long John Silver, the pirate of Treasure Island, has one wooden leg, so his gait is partly wooden

explanation.surface: A pirate's gait compared with old English architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudor houses have exposed wooden frames filled with plaster, a style described by this term.

clue.text: Beetle hunter using wrong end of forceps

indicators.note: using another letter here means it stands in for the letter it replaces

parts.note: a hunter is one who chases quarry, a chaser

indicators.note: the word forceps ends in S, so its wrong end is its opening letter, which takes the place of the S

explanation.surface: An entomologist grips a beetle with tweezers held the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using wrong end of forceps' swaps the S of CHASER (the right end of forceps) for F, its other end.
explanation.definitionFit: A chafer is a large beetle, such as the cockchafer or rose chafer.

clue.text: He loathes half-hearted party man

indicators.note: the doubled letters at the heart lose one of their two, halving the heart

parts.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A political party member feels lukewarm loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party man' suggests politics but is the Mad Hatter of the tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: One who loathes something is someone who hates, so 'he loathes' describes such a person.

clue.text: Bill's promises to pay after trip illusory

indicators.note: the account and the promises come after the trip

parts.note: to trip is to stumble, a fall
AC, account, is a bill; the apostrophe-s is possessive
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A man named Bill takes a tumble and his promised payments prove worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is AC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallacious means based on a false idea, misleading or deceptive, as illusory things are.

clue.text: Off-duty engineers making a fuss

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to create is a colloquial British word for making a fuss or complaining loudly

explanation.surface: Engineers grumble about their time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreating means enjoying recreation, leisure activity in free time away from work.

clue.text: Food bottles ornately cut on the inside

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed on the inside of the word for bottles

parts.note: vials are small glass bottles

indicators.note: worked ornately, the letters of cut are elaborately rearranged

explanation.surface: Fancy cut-glass bottles are decorated on their inner surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of the cut-glass picture, but it is the fodder that 'ornately' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Victuals is an old-fashioned word for provisions or things to eat.

clue.text: One-time literary heroine almost leaning over

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: almost the whole name, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Alice is Lewis Carroll's heroine in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A heroine from old novels is pictured nearly toppling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' reads as 'former' but splits into one and time; 'over' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so its letters are slanted rather than upright.

clue.text: Forcibly lift teapot to supply sustenance for diner

parts.note: to jack something is to raise it with a jack, a lifting device

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb, in a supple way, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone yanks a teapot up to serve food at a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb of supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked potato in its skin is a common cafe dish, food for someone eating out.

clue.text: Court linesman?

parts.note: not a tennis official but a writer of lines of verse attached to the royal court

explanation.surface: A tennis official calling shots at the edge of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's laureate is the monarch's appointed versifier, a writer of lines employed by the royal household.

clue.text: I tried exotic line carried by agent with enthusiasm

indicators.note: the pieces are held within the word for agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: exotic means strange and unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agent eagerly tries an unusual line of attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' turns I TRIED into IRITED; with L it is 'carried by' SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something spiritedly means doing it with energy and vigour.

clue.text: Transfer of power as Democrat replaces Republican in coup

indicators.note: replaces says one party's letter takes the place of the other's

parts.note: a revolution is the overthrow of a government, as a coup is

explanation.surface: A political shift as Democrats oust Republicans in an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Devolution is the delegation of governing authority from the centre to regions.

clue.text: Regularly cut prices? Try paying proper duty

indicators.note: cutting out every other letter, at regular intervals, leaves the first, third and fifth letters of each word

explanation.surface: A shopper slashing prices is urged to pay their taxes honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paying' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is dutiful reverence, as in filial piety, the proper respect owed to parents or God.

clue.text: Rough and ready needlewoman may

definitions.meaning: improvised, serving for the time being
a seamstress may sew up a shift, a simple dress or slip

explanation.surface: A crude seamstress at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A shift is a loose straight dress, so a needlewoman may make one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is a temporary, improvised substitute, crude but serviceable.

clue.text: Wealthy husband lacking in height ignoring a reprimand

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word for wealthy inside the other
ignoring means the letter A is left out of the word for height

parts.note: stature is a person's height

indicators.note: lacking means the word for wealthy goes without the letter for husband

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A rich, short husband is told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' cuts RICH to RIC; 'ignoring a' cuts STATURE to STTURE; RIC goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a sternly critical remark, a censure or rebuke.

clue.text: Long-term leader abandoned vote-loser

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A long-serving party leader finally ditches an unpopular colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D. Roosevelt won four presidential elections, the longest-serving US president.

clue.text: No good found in wayward northern city

indicators.note: no good means the word for wayward is left without its G

parts.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward, as in a rogue elephant

explanation.surface: Nothing worthwhile is to be found in some unruly city up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' looks like a description of the city but means drop G from ROGUE, leaving ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a city in Normandy, northern France, on the Seine.

clue.text: Explores classical author, including Catholic masterpieces

parts.note: to tour a place is to explore it

indicators.note: the author's name takes in the abbreviation for Catholic

parts.note: Daniel Defoe, author of the classic Robinson Crusoe
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Someone visits the works of an old writer, including religious masterworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical author' points to a writer of English classics, not Greek or Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour de force is a feat of great skill, an outstanding achievement or work.

clue.text: Fine riddle I penned in days before uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, uprising means the letters are read from the bottom up
the I is shut up inside the word for days before, as in a pen

parts.note: eves are the days before festivals or events

explanation.surface: A clever puzzle was written in the days leading up to a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned in' puts I inside EVES to make EVEIS, and 'uprising' turns that around. 'riddle' is not a puzzle here: it is a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse mesh for sifting soil; one with a fine mesh is the kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Gently carry wounded leader away from front

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: aft means towards the rear of a ship, away from the front

explanation.surface: An injured commander is carried tenderly from the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: To waft is to convey lightly through the air, as a breeze carries a scent.

clue.text: Some newlyweds getting up fresh in the morning?

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means the letters are read upwards
some of the word means a run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: Newlyweds rising bright and early after their wedding night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes YWED from 'newlyweds' and 'getting up' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew settles overnight, so grass is wet with it at dawn; the question mark flags this example.

clue.text: Rubbish left by side of road

indicators.note: by means next to, so the letter for left sits beside the drive

parts.note: a drive is a private road leading off the side of a public one

explanation.surface: Garbage dumped on the verge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly nonsense, talk that is worthless, as rubbish can mean.

clue.text: A short papal missive listed in gallery catalogue

indicators.note: the pieces are entered inside the name of the gallery, as an item is listed in a register

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a bull is a formal papal edict

explanation.surface: A papal letter appears in an art gallery's list of exhibits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts BULL to BUL; A BUL is 'listed in' TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tabulate is to arrange data in a table, so to catalogue or list systematically.

clue.text: American from East always remarkably keen

indicators.note: read from the east means from right to left, so the word is turned back

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always or ever

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of keen are strikingly rearranged

explanation.surface: An American from the eastern states is always unusually enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from East' reverses AY to YA; 'remarkably' rearranges KEEN to NKEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is a colloquial name for an American, especially one from New England.

clue.text: Fairly timid people at last coming aboard in the main

indicators.note: coming aboard means getting inside, as passengers board a ship

parts.note: in the main is an idiom for for the most part, generally

indicators.note: the final letters of the two words timid and people are taken

explanation.surface: Shy folk eventually board a ship on the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' picks D and E, which go 'coming aboard' MOSTLY. 'the main' suggests the sea, but it is part of an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Modestly priced goods are fairly priced, reasonable in a moderate, unextravagant way.
